children: Nomura expects GE Vernova T&D India, Hitachi Energy India and CG Power to be the major beneficiaries of the government's Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III), saying the significantly higher outlay and addition targets could provide tailwinds to the transmission capex cycle.
The brokerage has a 'Buy' rating on all three stocks.

"the sharply higher outlay, addition targets, CFA and inclusion of the BESS component under GEC-III boosts the demand visibility for transmission equipment manufacturers and players providing BESS solutions," Nomura said in a September 30 report.

The Union Cabinet approved GEC-III on September 30, with a total outlay of Rs 1.9 trillion. The scheme aims to evacuate 135 GW of renewable energy and deploy 50 GWh of battery energy storage systems (BESS).

Of the total outlay, Rs 1.4 trillion will be allocated to the intra-state transmission system (ISTS), while Rs 0.5 trillion will go towards BESS. The scheme will receive central financial assistance of Rs 541 billion, or 29% of the total outlay, and is targeted for completion by FY33.
Nomura said GEC-III marks a "sharp step-up" from the earlier phases in terms of outlay and expects additions of transmission lines and substations to be substantially higher.

GEC-I, announced in FY16, had a total outlay of Rs 101 billion and targeted 24 GW of renewable energy integration. GEC-II, announced in FY22, had an outlay of Rs 120 billion and targeted 20 GW. GEC-III, announced in FY27, has a significantly larger outlay of Rs 1,864 billion and a 135 GW renewable energy integration target.

Nomura noted that the execution track record of earlier phases has been mixed. While GEC-I largely achieved its targets after its completion deadline was extended to March 2023, GEC-II had 73 of 91 packages tendered and 67 awarded as of December 2025, but no renewable energy projects had been connected under the scheme, according to information provided by states.

The brokerage also said greenfield projects under GEC-III will be awarded through the tariff-based competitive bidding (TBCB) route, which it believes is likely to benefit private transmission companies.

title: GE Vernova T&D India, Hitachi Energy India, CG Power to benefit from GEC-III: Nomura
